serviceIdentification.serviceDescription: The RegScale Trust Center is an automated Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) offering built for FedRAMP 20x and CR26. It delivers continuous controls monitoring and publishes a FedRAMP-compatible trust center that meets every FedRAMP 20x provider rule, generating schema-valid, machine-readable evidence directly from live security posture and republishing automatically on change.

trustCenter.accessRequestInstructions: Agencies and authorized parties request access to RegScale Trust Center certification materials through the public Trust Center at https://trust.regscale.com. Public certification-package data (CPO, Secure Configuration Guide, and KSI summaries) is available without an account; controlled or detailed materials require an access request submitted through the Trust Center, which the RegScale security team reviews and approves.

secureConfigurationGuidance.usageInstructions: Fetch the machine-readable guide from this URL (no authentication required); a human-readable rendering is served alongside it at /api/v1/fedramp/20x/systems/trust-center-20x-class-c/scg.md. Each section carries the setting, its hardened value, and verification steps — apply the settings for your deployment model and re-check after provider releases, which are versioned and announced through the published release history.

significantChangeNotificationMechanism.description: Significant changes are evaluated against the CR26 change types, approved in-app, and notified to each recorded recipient (FedRAMP, agencies) with per-recipient delivery state. Every CR26 notification window is tracked as a business-day obligation with automated reminders; late notices are permanently flagged in the history and audit feeds.

serviceProperties.perServiceMaterialsExplanation: RegScale does not supply separate per-service certification materials. The offering is a single consolidated service with one authorization boundary, so the full certification package covers it in one comprehensive set rather than per-service breakouts, aligned with the control note. This discretionary (MAY) decision was reviewed and signed off by Cory Henrickson, RegScale.
